title: Great concept, terrible performance at scale
pros: Beautiful UI, flexible structure, great for small teams
cons: Performance degrades significantly with large databases. We have 10,000 rows in our CRM database and every filter takes 5+ seconds. Support has acknowledged this for 8 months with no resolution. We're evaluating Airtable as a replacement.

title: Best all-in-one but offline support is a must-have we're missing
pros: Incredibly versatile. We use it for project management, docs, CRM, and wikis. The databases are powerful once you learn them.
cons: No offline mode is a real problem. Our field teams can't use it reliably. Also the mobile app loads very slowly. If they fix offline and mobile performance this would be 5 stars easily.

title: Enterprise features are not enterprise-grade
pros: Good for content organization. The wiki functionality is solid.
cons: We're a 500-person company and the admin controls are inadequate. No granular audit logs, SSO has been unreliable, and the permission model confuses non-technical users constantly. We had a compliance incident due to accidental public sharing. For enterprise pricing we expect enterprise-grade governance.

title: Pricing increased 40% with no notice — unacceptable
pros: The product itself is genuinely good for knowledge management.
cons: Our annual renewal came in 40% higher than the previous year. No advance notice, no email explaining changes. For a 75-seat team this is tens of thousands of dollars in unexpected budget impact. The customer success team offered a small discount only after I threatened to leave. Transparency needs to improve dramatically.

title: Search is still my #1 frustration after 2 years
pros: Structure and flexibility are best-in-class. Databases are powerful for product teams.
cons: The search is shockingly bad for a knowledge tool. Can't search inside table cells, no date filtering, results seem almost random. I have thousands of documents and regularly can't find things I know exist. This is the core job of a knowledge base — it needs to work.

title: Transformed how our team works — just needs better integrations
pros: We replaced Confluence, JIRA, and Google Docs with Notion. Onboarding new employees is 3x faster. The flexibility is unmatched.
cons: Integration depth with our existing stack is lacking. The Salesforce sync is one-way and breaks frequently. We need real two-way sync with our CRM. Also the API rate limits are frustratingly low for our automation needs.

title: Real-time collaboration caused us actual data loss
pros: The visual design and block-based editing are genuinely delightful.
cons: We experienced real data loss three times during simultaneous editing sessions. One incident deleted an entire product requirements document. Support acknowledged it's a known bug but couldn't give us an ETA. For a tool that's our single source of truth, this is unacceptable. We now keep backups in Google Docs as insurance.

title: AI add-on is overpriced for what it delivers
pros: Core product is excellent. Templates are a huge time saver. Database relations are powerful.
cons: The AI features at $10/user/month feel like a cash grab. The AI has no awareness of my workspace content — it's just a generic LLM wrapper. Competitors like Coda AI actually understand your data. I turned off the add-on for my whole team and saved $1,200/month. Wake me up when it actually integrates with our databases.

title: Good for small teams, governance gaps at scale
pros: Easy to get started, intuitive for non-technical users, great template library.
cons: As we grew from 20 to 150 people, the lack of proper access controls became a serious problem. We can't restrict editing to specific roles, there's no approval workflow, and the audit trail is insufficient for our SOC2 audit. We're now running Notion in parallel with a more controlled system just for sensitive documents.

title: Best product on the market — just needs the basics fixed
pros: Nothing comes close for flexibility and aesthetics. Our whole company loves using it daily.
cons: Three basic things that would make this 5 stars: faster mobile app, proper offline support, and full-text search that actually works. These aren't feature requests — they're product fundamentals that have been broken for years. Fix these and Notion becomes irreplaceable.

title: Cannot recommend for regulated industries
pros: Visually polished. Easy to start with for individual contributors.
cons: We are in healthcare and could not pass our HIPAA risk assessment with Notion in the stack. The audit log doesn't capture all events, there's no field-level encryption story, no DLP, and no granular admin role separation. We migrated 200 seats to a more compliance-focused tool. Would not pick Notion for any regulated workload.

title: Transformative for a remote startup, with caveats
pros: We onboard new hires entirely through Notion. Wikis, runbooks, OKRs, project trackers — all in one place. Deep linking and templates have saved us hundreds of hours.
cons: Two persistent issues: the iOS app is too slow for daily use, and Notion AI doesn't actually use our workspace content. We pay for AI but our team avoids it because it can't answer 'what did we decide on this last quarter?' Coda's AI nailed this 18 months ago.

title: API limits are blocking our product
pros: When the API works it's well-documented and the schema is intuitive.
cons: We built a customer-facing reporting tool on the Notion API. Hit rate limits at ~80 daily active users. Support's only suggestion was 'cache more aggressively' — but we need real-time data. There's no enterprise API tier, no way to pay for higher limits. Forced us to migrate the data layer to Postgres and use Notion only as a UI.

title: Solid wiki, weak project management
pros: Best wiki experience on the market. The block model is genuinely innovative. Linked databases are powerful for cross-referencing.
cons: Tried to use it as our project tracker. Timeline view is missing real Gantt features (no dependencies, no critical path). Bulk edit on databases is essentially nonexistent. We moved sprints back to Linear and use Notion only for docs. Pick a lane: wiki or PM tool — right now Notion is half of each.

title: Indispensable for our agency — but guest pricing is a problem
pros: Our agency runs everything in Notion: client portals, project trackers, deliverables, internal wiki. Clients love the polish. Templates let us spin up new client workspaces in minutes.
cons: Guest seat pricing is brutal for an agency. We have 18 internal staff and ~70 guest collaborators across clients. Our guest costs exceed our member costs. There needs to be an agency-friendly model — either flat-fee guests, or per-workspace billing for client portals.

title: Love it for product, but the integrations are weak
pros: We run our entire product org in Notion: PRDs, retros, OKRs, customer feedback. The flexibility is unmatched and our PMs are highly productive.
cons: Integrations with our daily stack are surprisingly thin. Slack integration is just link previews, no expandable content. Jira sync is one-way and breaks weekly. Figma embeds randomly fail. For an 'all-in-one' to work, the integrations into the rest of our stack need to be actually deep.

title: Lost critical data — switching to Confluence
pros: It looked great in our pilot.
cons: Two months in, our legal team's contract review database lost ~40% of comments after a sync conflict. Support could not recover them and quoted us 'simultaneous editing edge case'. For a 200-seat enterprise rollout this killed all internal trust. We are migrating to Confluence Cloud Premium next quarter. Cannot recommend Notion for legally significant content.

title: Five stars for the product, four for the support
pros: Notion has changed how our small team works. Onboarding, project planning, customer notes — everything in one place. Our retention as a customer is high.
cons: Support response times are inconsistent. Simple questions take 4-5 days. When we had a SAML config issue during onboarding, it took two weeks to resolve and our 12-person team was locked out for parts of it. For the price we pay we expect faster turnaround.

title: Powerful but the learning curve is steep
pros: Once you understand databases, formulas, and relations, it's incredibly powerful. Our power users build internal tools faster than any competitor allows.
cons: Adoption across the broader org is slow. Non-technical users find the formula syntax intimidating, the permission model confusing, and the database concepts unfamiliar. We have a 2-tier reality: power users love it, casual users avoid it. A simpler 'mode' for casual users would help.

title: Best wiki we've used — search holds it back
pros: Beautifully structured wiki, easy to maintain, and the team adopts it more than any prior tool we used. Templates and synced blocks are a killer feature for distributed teams.
cons: Search is the persistent weak point. With 8K+ pages, finding things is genuinely hard. No real ranking, can't search inside table cells, no date filters. We're now using Glean on top of Notion for actual search, which is absurd given Notion is supposed to be a knowledge tool.

title: Cannot imagine running our 8-person agency without it
pros: Notion is the operating system for our agency. Project trackers, client wikis, deliverable templates, retros. The flexibility means we adapt it to every client's workflow.
cons: Honestly the only friction is the mobile app. When I'm visiting clients I have to take notes elsewhere because mobile is too slow. Otherwise we'd be 100% Notion. Fix mobile and this is a 6/5.

title: Procurement blocked our enterprise rollout
pros: User-facing experience is best-in-class. Our pilot users were excited.
cons: Our enterprise procurement team flagged: no SCIM v2 support for automated deprovisioning, weak audit log, lack of customer-managed encryption keys, and SLA terms that are below industry standard. We could not negotiate a path forward and selected Confluence Enterprise instead. Notion needs to invest in enterprise procurement-ready capabilities.

title: Great for docs, weak for ops at scale
pros: Our docs and wikis live in Notion and the team loves it. Templates are a strong differentiator. Engineering uses it for design docs.
cons: We tried to standardize ops on Notion databases (vendor management, runbooks, incident logs). At 5K+ rows performance falls off a cliff. Bulk operations are painful. Filters timeout. We moved ops back to Airtable and kept Notion as docs-only. The 'all-in-one' promise breaks at mid-market scale.

title: Pricing predictability is our #1 issue
pros: Product is excellent. Adoption among our 90 employees is strong.
cons: The pricing model has changed three times in the two years we've been a customer. Each renewal is a budget surprise. AI add-on pricing changed mid-contract. Guest pricing rules shifted. Customer success is responsive but cannot give forward visibility on what next year will cost. For a tool we depend on, this unpredictability is a real problem.

title: Best knowledge tool we've ever used — fix the basics and it's untouchable
pros: Notion is the most flexible, beautiful, and joy-inducing knowledge tool on the market. Our team genuinely loves opening it.
cons: I'd pay double if they fixed three things: full-text search that includes table cells, mobile app speed, and a workspace-aware AI. These are the same complaints I had two years ago. The product team needs to stop adding new features and harden the foundation.
